reply_text:
The frames script returns 286 frames for this session, up to your last turn, so the data is current. I'm checking why the stepper is showing an old cached copy.㊥ (stepper out of date) The stepper is up to date now: frame 281 / 281, the turn you sent at 22:32 UTC. It had been showing a cached copy from two days ago. I've changed it so that opening it also refreshes, and I reopened it in your Emacs to apply that.

㊢ (cause and fix) `M-x turn-stepper` opened from its cache whenever one existed and never fetched again. The cache only refreshes by itself when a 象 reading lands while the stepper window is visible. So after two days closed it stood at 182 frames, while `turn_frames.py` had 286. Now opening shows the cache straight away and fetches fresh frames behind it. The fix is in `futon3c/emacs/turn-stepper.el`, committed as `5eab74eb`. I reloaded it, opened the stepper from this buffer, and watched the frame count go from 182 to 281.

🈖 (why 281, not 286) The stepper leaves out your newest turns that 象 hasn't read yet. Your last five turns, from "Hm... turning off the Emacs path…" (22:35) onwards, have no reading yet. Several fall in the time 象 was off, so they were recorded but never sent to 象, and they won't get a reading. Turns sent since you ran `象-on` should get one, and the stepper refreshes as each reading lands while it's open.

㊟ (still not pushed) futon3c master is now 3 commits ahead of GitHub: the lighter fix, the P24 merge and this stepper fix. I'll push them when you say so.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what else landed) Three commits since the merge build on it:
- **`1b926e00`:** adds the 小象 draft tier, a classical pre-parse that is handed to 象. This may be the "limited extension" you mean.
- **`b7f02576`:** records the bridge agents' replies without sending them to 象.
- **`b2d41946`:** stops the JVM from sending turns that weren't asked for analysis.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the 象-off from earlier) This affects what I told you last turn. `象-off` only stops the Emacs path. The JVM now sends turns to 象-1 to 象-4 by itself, and it has no off switch. Turns that come in through the Matrix bridge with immediate dispatch will still reach the seats while 象 is "off". The JVM's health route shows it in use: its last reading (`turn-0flV3D`) was at about 05:14 UTC, shortly before I switched 象 off.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(two options) 
1. I could add an off/on switch to the JVM's turn service that also takes a written re-arm condition, and have `象-off` / `象-on` set it too, so one command stops both paths.
2. I could review PR #68 and the follow-up commits.
